The Secretary of State considers there are reasonable grounds to suspect the company is an 'involved person' due to its involvement in destabilizing Ukraine or undermining its territorial integrity, sovereignty, or independence. This includes making available economic resources, goods, or technology that could contribute to these actions.

The company is now subject to an asset freeze, trust services sanctions, and director disqualification sanctions. This action highlights the UK's continued efforts to target entities supporting Russia's aggression against Ukraine.

articles.headline: U.S. Annual Inflation Holds at 3.4% in August; Euro Area Inflation Projected to Remain Above Target
body: The annual inflation rate in the United States remained at 3.4% for the 12 months ending August 2026, consistent with July's figures, according to data released by the U.S. Labor Department on September 11, 2026. The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) increased 0.4% on a seasonally adjusted basis in August.

Meanwhile, the European Central Bank (ECB) announced on September 10, 2026, that it expects headline inflation in the euro area to average 3.0% in 2026, 2.5% in 2027, and 2.1% in 2028. Inflation excluding energy and food is projected at 2.5% in 2026, 2.6% in 2027, and 2.3% in 2028.

The ECB noted that the conflict in the Middle East continues to generate inflation pressures, and inflation is set to remain well above its 2% target for an extended period. In the U.S., the August CPI report more or less assures a Federal Reserve rate hike in September, as the economy remains strong enough to support such a move.
articles.source: U.S. Labor Department / European Central Bank

articles.headline: Global Bond Sell-Off Continues, Pushing Yields to Multi-Year Highs
body: A widespread sell-off in government bonds has continued this month, driving borrowing costs to multi-year highs across major economies. This broad market movement has increased pressure on governments, companies, and households globally.

Bloomberg reports that global bond yields reached their highest level in almost two decades in early September. Notably, Japan's 10-year government bond yield surpassed 3% for the first time since 1996, while German and French benchmark yields climbed to their highest in over a decade.

Several factors are contributing to this rise, including renewed concerns that inflation could persist due to higher energy prices, making rapid interest rate cuts less likely. Governments are also issuing more debt, and large technology companies are increasing borrowing to finance investments in AI and digital infrastructure.

articles.headline: US Annual Inflation Rate Holds Steady at 3.4% in August 2026
body: The annual inflation rate in the United States remained unchanged at 3.4% in August 2026, matching the July reading and aligning with forecasts. This data point indicates a stabilization in the overall pace of price increases.

A closer look at the components reveals that gasoline prices saw a significant year-over-year increase of 27.4%, slightly higher than the 24.6% rise in July. Fuel oil prices also surged by 52%, compared to 39.1% in the previous month.

Conversely, inflation eased for shelter, decreasing from 3.2% to 3%, and for food, which slowed from 3% to 2.7%. On a monthly basis, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose by 0.4%, primarily driven by a 3.9% increase in gasoline prices, which accounted for over one-third of the monthly rise.
articles.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics / Trading Economics

articles.headline: U.S. Consumer Price Index Rises 3.4% Year-Over-Year in August, Driven by Energy
body: The U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) increased by 0.4% in August on a seasonally adjusted basis, following a 0.1% rise in July, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.
Over the last 12 months, the all-items index increased 3.4% before seasonal adjustment, with energy prices surging 16.3% from August 2025 to August 2026.

The volatile mix of a widening Iran war pushing oil prices near $100 a barrel, increased tariffs, and significant AI spending contributing to higher chip and memory prices are all keeping upward pressure on consumer prices.
articles.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics / National Apartment Association

articles.headline: U.S. Inflation Remains Elevated in August Amid Energy Price Surge
body: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) in the United States increased by 0.4% in August on a seasonally adjusted basis, following a 0.1% rise in July, with the annual inflation rate holding steady at 3.4%.

Energy prices were a significant driver, with the energy index jumping 16.3% year-over-year, primarily due to a 27.4% increase in gasoline and a 52.0% gain in fuel oil, exacerbated by the ongoing conflict in Iran and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.
Core inflation, excluding food and energy, rose 2.4% year-over-year, a slight deceleration from previous months, but overall price pressures continue to strain consumers and housing markets.
articles.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics / National Apartment Association / Trading Economics

articles.headline: OCC Proposes Tailored Third-Party Risk Management Guidance for Community Banks
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) announced on September 11, 2026, a proposal to tailor third-party risk management guidance, aiming to reduce the burden on community banks. This initiative is part of the OCC's broader effort to empower community banks and streamline regulatory requirements.

The proposed guidance would allow banks to focus their resources on third-party relationships based on the magnitude and likelihood of potential harm, moving away from overly broad, process-driven approaches. It emphasizes that there is no one-size-fits-all approach to third-party risk management and encourages responsible innovation.

This action follows previous OCC efforts to rightsize regulatory burden, including creating a distinct line of supervision for community banks and tailoring examination scope and frequency. The OCC also provided clarity regarding the agency's risk-based supervision and enforcement of core service providers.

articles.headline: Security Council, 10218th Meeting (AM) Iran
body: At 10 a.m., the Security Council will hold a briefing on the work of the 1737 Sanctions Committee concerning Iran, to be convened by France, Council President for September, under the "Non-Proliferation" agenda item. The 1737 Sanctions Committee was established by resolution 1737 (2006), with a requirement to report to the Council every 90 days. Prior to the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) on Iran’s nuclear programme, which the Council endorsed through resolution 2231 (2015), these briefings took place every three months under the “Non-Proliferation” agenda item. Resolution 2231 (2015) had suspended all prior sanctions resolutions on Iran, including resolution 1737 (2006), rendering the 1737 Committee and its reporting requirement defunct. In August 2025, France, Germany and the United Kingdom - the "E3" parties to the JCPOA - then triggered the agreement's "snapback" mechanism to reimpose UN sanctions on Iran.

These actions are part of the U.S. Department of the Treasury-led 'Operation Economic Outcast.'

Under the updated licensing policy, Iran-related specific license applications will now be treated with a presumption of denial, except as required by law or in certain circumstances, such as risk to life, limb, or environmental safety.

The Counter Terrorism designations target networks enabling the Iranian regime's terrorist proxies, including entities and individuals supporting Kata'ib Hizballah and Lebanese Hizballah. articles.headline: EU Strengthens Russia Sanctions with 20th and 21st Packages, Targets War Economy
body: The European Union has further strengthened its sanctions policy against Russia in 2026, adopting the 20th and 21st sanctions packages in response to Russia's ongoing war of aggression against Ukraine, war crimes, internal repression, and malicious cyber activities.

The 21st sanctions package, adopted in July, is the largest EU sanctions listings package in four years, targeting the financial backbone of Russia's war machine. This includes the shadow fleet, banks, crypto-asset networks, oil revenues, refineries, military-industrial entities, and sanctions circumvention channels.

These measures aim to weaken Russia's ability to wage war, protect European security, and ensure accountability for those responsible for aggression and violations of international law. Western sanctions have already cost Russia an estimated €1.3 trillion.

body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related and Counter Terrorism designations, signaling a continued focus on disrupting illicit financial networks. This policy shift significantly tightens the authorization process for transactions involving Iran, expanding secondary-sanctions risks for those operating in or supporting the aviation, digital-asset, gold, shipping, and technology sectors.

articles.headline: ECB Hikes Rates by 25 Basis Points Amid Persistent Inflationary Pressures
body: The European Central Bank (ECB) Governing Council today decided to raise its three key interest rates by 25 basis points. This decision comes as the conflict in the Middle East continues to generate inflationary pressures, and inflation is projected to remain well above target for an extended period.

The ECB's new staff projections forecast headline inflation to average 3.0% in 2026, 2.5% in 2027, and 2.1% in 2028. The baseline projection for inflation excluding energy and food is 2.5% in 2026, 2.6% in 2027, and 2.3% in 2028, with upward revisions for 2027 and 2028 compared to June.

The Governing Council reiterated its commitment to a data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting approach, with future interest rate decisions based on the inflation outlook, incoming economic and financial data, underlying inflation dynamics, and the strength of monetary policy transmission.

articles.headline: Federal Reserve Signals Continued Vigilance on Inflation Amidst Mixed Economic Data
body: Federal Reserve officials continue to emphasize a data-dependent approach to monetary policy, with recent statements indicating a sustained focus on bringing inflation down to the 2% target. While some economic indicators show signs of cooling, the labor market remains robust, presenting a complex picture for policymakers.

Analysts suggest that the Fed is likely to maintain its cautious stance, closely monitoring upcoming inflation reports and employment figures before making any significant policy shifts. The possibility of further interest rate adjustments remains on the table if inflationary pressures persist.

Market participants are keenly watching for any forward guidance from the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) regarding the future trajectory of interest rates, as the central bank navigates the delicate balance between controlling inflation and supporting economic growth.

This marks the second rate hike by the ECB this year, with markets pricing in at least one further increase by year-end and a deposit rate potentially exceeding 3% in 2027.

The ECB's hawkish stance is largely attributed to rising energy prices, which are threatening to keep inflation elevated despite some economists anticipating a potential dampening effect on economic growth.

articles.headline: UN Security Council Debates Iran Sanctions Amid Divisions Over 'Snapback' Mechanism
body: The UN Security Council held a briefing on the 1737 Sanctions Committee concerning Iran, with significant divisions emerging among member states regarding the legal validity of the 'snapback' mechanism that reimposed UN sanctions in August 2025. China and Russia opposed the adoption of a formal committee report, arguing that Resolution 2231 expired on October 18, 2025.

France, Germany, and the United Kingdom, who triggered the snapback, maintain that six Security Council resolutions on Iran, including Resolution 1737, have been back in force for nearly a year. They assert that Iran has expanded its nuclear program in ways that lack credible civilian justification.

The debate highlights the ongoing international disagreement over the status of Iran's nuclear program and the effectiveness of UN sanctions, with the 1737 Committee's substantive work remaining blocked due to these disputes.
articles.source: UN Meetings Coverage and Press Releases / Reuters

articles.headline: US-Cuba Talks Stall Amidst Fresh Sanctions and Threats Against the Island
body: Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla revealed that the U.S. and Cuba are not currently engaged in talks to end the enduring diplomatic crisis between the two nations. This cessation of dialogue is a recent development, as Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel had announced in March that negotiations were underway to de-escalate bilateral tensions.

Since January, the Trump administration has repeatedly threatened the Cuban leadership with regime change and tightened punitive sanctions on the island. This includes a near-complete blockade of oil imports since January, causing repeated nationwide blackouts.

Various sectors of the Cuban economy and figures associated with the governing Cuban Communist Party have been targeted, including the recent U.S. State Department sanctions against Fidel Ernesto Castro, the grandson of former Cuban President Raúl Castro, and various Cuban companies associated with their energy, mining, and banking sectors.

articles.headline: FinCEN Assesses $125 Million Civil Penalty Against UBS Financial Services Inc.
body: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has assessed a $125,000,000 civil money penalty against UBS Financial Services Inc. (UBSFS) for willful violations of the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA).

This significant penalty, which is the largest ever imposed on a broker-dealer for BSA violations, stems from UBSFS's deficient AML policies, procedures, and internal controls, leading to a failure to monitor tens of thousands of transactions and file suspicious activity reports.
The severity of the penalty is partly due to UBSFS being a recidivist, having resolved similar charges in 2018 and failing to complete promised remediation.
articles.source: FinCEN / Hedge Fund Law Report / Axle Blog

These import bans are set to take effect on September 29, 2026, with product additions and removals effective September 15, 2026. The U.S. aims to protect American farmers, manufacturers, and workers by addressing Canada's retaliatory and discriminatory practices.

articles.headline: FinCEN Identifies $17.5 Billion in Suspected Health Care Fraud
body: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has identified approximately $17.5 billion in suspicious financial activity potentially linked to health care fraud. This finding is based on an analysis of over 5,700 Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) reports filed by financial institutions between March 1, 2025, and February 28, 2026.

The suspected schemes involved Medicare, Medicaid, and private insurance, with potentially fraudulent funds often originating from a combination of federal and state programs and private insurers. Home health care businesses accounted for the largest share of suspected fraudulent providers, appearing in 20% of health care fraud-related BSA reports.

This financial intelligence provides law enforcement with critical insights to identify, investigate, and disrupt illicit schemes that exploit taxpayer-funded health care benefits, underscoring the Treasury Department's commitment to combating fraud.
articles.source: FinCEN / U.S. Department of the Treasury

body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced a sweeping action under 'Operation Economic Outcast,' sanctioning 36 targets for their support of Iran's aviation sector. This move aims to cripple the regime's ability to transport weapons, personnel, and illicit cargo globally.

The sanctions also target covert front companies, foreign intermediaries, and deceptive transshipment routes that Iran utilizes to acquire U.S.-origin aircraft and sensitive technology. Concurrently, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has issued an Alert urging financial institutions to report any procurement networks supporting Iran's aviation industry.

As part of this action, OFAC is suspending three Iran-related aviation authorizations, which previously allowed for overflights and permitted non-U.S. airlines to operate U.S.-origin or U.S.-controlled commercial aircraft into Iran. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that any foreign entity or individual enabling sanctioned Iranian airlines will face severe consequences and risk being cut off from the global financial system.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-Related and Counter-Terrorism Designations, Amends General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has implemented new sanctions targeting entities and individuals connected to Iran and those involved in counter-terrorism activities. These designations are part of ongoing efforts to pressure Iran's illicit financial activities and support for terrorism.

Alongside these new designations, OFAC updated several Iran-related General Licenses and issued a new Counter Terrorism General License. These amendments aim to clarify authorized transactions and provide specific guidance for certain activities, while maintaining a robust sanctions framework.
Separately, FinCEN issued an alert to counter Iranian procurement efforts for its commercial aviation industry.

articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions Iran's Aviation Sector, Suspends Key General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related and counter terrorism designations, targeting Iran's aviation sector under 'Operation Economic Outcast'.

OFAC suspended several key Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations (ITSR) General Licenses, including GL J-1, which previously authorized the reexportation of certain civil aircraft to Iran on temporary sojourn, and authorizations for payments for overflights of Iranian airspace, bunkering, and emergency repairs.

To facilitate an orderly wind-down, OFAC issued Counter Terrorism General License 37 and Iran General License DD, authorizing the wind-down of certain transactions previously permitted under the suspended authorizations until September 23, 2026.

articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions Iranian Aviation Sector, Suspends General Licenses, and Issues New Counter Terrorism License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has implemented sweeping sanctions targeting Iran's aviation sector, designating 35 entities and one individual for supporting the sector, which is allegedly used to transport weapons, military personnel, and illicit cargo. This action is part of 'Operation Economic Outcast.'

OFAC suspended Iran General License J-1, which previously authorized the temporary reexportation of certain civil aircraft to Iran, as well as authorizations for overflights of Iranian airspace, bunkering, and emergency repairs.

In conjunction with these measures, OFAC issued Counter Terrorism General License 37, authorizing a wind-down period for transactions involving certain designated persons until September 23, 2026. Additionally, Iran General License DD was issued to authorize the wind-down of certain civil aviation-related and other transactions previously permitted under the Iranian Transactions and Sanctions Regulations.

body: OFAC has announced new Iran-related and Counter Terrorism designations, targeting entities and individuals involved in supporting illicit activities.

These actions follow OFAC's recent sanctions against Türkiye-based Golden Global Bank and two subsidiaries for Iran-related financial-sector activity and correspondent-banking support.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-Related and Counter-Terrorism Designations, Updates General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related and counter-terrorism designations on September 8, 2026, as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast.' These actions target networks, facilitators, and financial channels used by Iran to smuggle oil, evade sanctions, and fund terrorist activities.

The designations also included entities and individuals supporting Iran's aviation sector, specifically targeting covert front companies, foreign intermediaries, and deceptive transshipment routes used to acquire U.S.-origin aircraft and sensitive technology. OFAC warned that any entity facilitating money laundering or sanctions evasion for Iran risks being cut off from the U.S. financial system.

In addition to the new designations, OFAC updated several Iran-related General Licenses and issued a new Counter Terrorism General License. Notably, Iran General License J-1, which permitted the reexportation of certain civil aircraft to Iran on temporary sojourn, has been indefinitely suspended. OFAC also issued Iran General License DD, authorizing a wind-down period for transactions covered by the suspended authorizations until September 23, 2026.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related and Counter Terrorism Designations, Updates General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) today announced new Iran-related and Counter Terrorism designations, targeting entities and individuals involved in activities contrary to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. These actions reinforce the U.S. commitment to combating terrorism and restricting Iran's access to the international financial system.

In addition to the designations, OFAC issued updates to existing Iran-related General Licenses and a new Counter Terrorism General License. These licensing adjustments aim to provide clarity and, where appropriate, authorize certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under the sanctions programs.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related and Counter-Terrorism Designations, Updates General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) implemented new Iran-related designations and counter-terrorism designations. body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related and counter-terrorism designations as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' targeting Iran's aviation sector and other support networks. This action includes the designation of 27 Iranian airlines and numerous foreign intermediaries.

OFAC has also suspended several Iran-related General Licenses, including Iran General License J-1, which previously authorized the reexportation of certain civil aircraft to Iran on temporary sojourn. A new Counter Terrorism General License 37 has been issued, authorizing the wind-down of transactions involving certain newly blocked persons.

The designations target individuals and entities providing support to Mahan Air and other Iranian aviation activities, with companies based in the UAE, UK, Turkey, Malaysia, and Kazakhstan being impacted. This move aims to further isolate Iran's aviation sector from the global financial system.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Sweeping Sanctions on Iran's Aviation Sector, Updates General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced a series of Iran-related and counter-terrorism designations, significantly targeting Iran's civil aviation sector under 'Operation Economic Outcast'.

As part of this action, OFAC indefinitely suspended three general licenses (J-1, 31 CFR § 560.522, and 31 CFR § 560.523) that previously authorized certain civil aviation-related transactions with Iran. This means that the operation of flights to Iran using aircraft subject to U.S. jurisdiction is now prohibited, and payments for overflights of Iranian airspace or emergency landings will require specific licenses after September 23, 2026.

Concurrently, OFAC issued Iran General License DD, authorizing a wind-down period for transactions previously covered by the suspended general licenses until September 23, 2026. Additionally, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issued an alert to the commercial aviation industry, urging financial institutions to identify and report procurement networks supporting Iran's aviation industry.

articles.headline: UK Lays Legislation to Tackle Iranian Nuclear and Hostile Activity, Expands Sectoral Measures
body: The UK government has laid legislation to tackle Iranian nuclear activity and other hostile Iranian actions, citing Iran's lack of transparency regarding its nuclear program as a serious threat to international peace and security.

The new legislation, 'The Iran (Sanctions) (Amendment) Regulations 2026,' amends existing regulations to introduce sectoral measures broadly similar to those lifted as part of the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action.

These measures will further reduce the Government of Iran's ability to access the UK financial system and raise funds for its nuclear program. Trade prohibitions are expanded to include additional goods, technology, and services critical to Iranian nuclear escalation, such as energy, software, metals, gold, and related activities like shipping, insurance, and banking.

articles.headline: OFAC Grounds Iranian Airlines with Sweeping Sanctions, Suspends Aviation General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has imposed sweeping sanctions on 36 targets supporting Iran's aviation sector, including 27 Iranian airlines, as part of Operation Economic Outcast. This action aims to isolate Iran's aviation industry, which the regime uses for moving weapons, personnel, and illicit cargo.

OFAC also targeted eight third-country entities and one individual for facilitating Mahan Air's proliferation activities and illicit procurement of U.S.-origin aircraft. Concurrently, OFAC suspended three Iran-related aviation authorizations, including General License J-1, which previously allowed non-U.S. airlines to operate scheduled flights to and from Iran using U.S.-origin aircraft.

The suspensions also include authorizations for payments for overflights of Iranian airspace and a licensing policy for aircraft safety. The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issued an alert urging financial institutions to report procurement networks supporting Iran's aviation industry.

body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has imposed new Iran-related and counter-terrorism designations, significantly impacting Iran's aviation sector. In a major policy shift, OFAC indefinitely suspended Iran General License J-1, which previously authorized the reexportation of certain civil aircraft to Iran on temporary sojourn, as well as related transactions for overflights, bunkering, and emergency repairs. This suspension, effective September 8, 2026, aims to further isolate Iran's aviation industry from the global financial system.

Additionally, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issued an alert to the commercial aviation industry, urging U.S. financial institutions to identify and report procurement networks supporting Iran's aviation sector.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related and Counter Terrorism Designations, Suspends Key General Licenses for Aviation Sector

Concurrently, OFAC issued Iran General License DD, providing a wind-down period until September 23, 2026, for transactions previously authorized under the suspended licenses. These actions were taken pursuant to Executive Order 13224 (counterterrorism authority) and Executive Order 13902 (targeting sectors of the Iranian economy), with a particular focus on Iran's aviation sector.

OFAC also updated several Iran-related General Licenses and issued a new Counter-Terrorism General License, providing specific authorizations and guidance for certain transactions. This follows the indefinite suspension of three general licenses related to civil aviation on the same day.

These updates aim to clarify the scope of authorized activities and ensure that humanitarian and other permissible transactions can continue while maintaining pressure on designated parties.

articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions Iran's Aviation Sector, Designates Counter Terrorism Entities, and Updates General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced a significant sanctions action targeting Iran's aviation sector as part of Operation Economic Outcast. This action includes the designation of 36 targets, comprising 27 Iranian airlines, foreign intermediaries, cargo service providers, general sales agents, and companies allegedly involved in facilitating the transfer of U.S.-origin aircraft and aviation-related goods to Iran.

Concurrently, OFAC designated several counter terrorism entities and individuals for supporting Kata'ib Hizballah (KH) and Hizballah, which aid Iran in evading sanctions and collaborate with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force.

OFAC also announced the suspension of three Iran-related aviation authorizations, including General License J-1, which had authorized the reexportation of certain civil aircraft to Iran on temporary sojourn. Additionally, OFAC issued a new Counter Terrorism General License and updated several Iran-related General Licenses, including a temporary license for wind-down activities through September 23, 2026.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran and Counter Terrorism Designations; Updates Iran-Related General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related and Counter Terrorism designations, alongside significant updates to Iran-related General Licenses (GLs). These actions are part of an intensified campaign to isolate the Iranian regime and disrupt its illicit activities.

OFAC indefinitely suspended three Iran-related aviation general licenses (31 CFR § 560.522, 31 CFR § 560.529, and Iran GL J-1), which previously authorized certain transactions related to overflights of Iranian airspace, bunkering and emergency repairs for non-Iranian carriers, and the reexportation of certain civil aircraft to Iran on temporary sojourn.

In conjunction with these suspensions, OFAC issued Counter Terrorism General License 37 and Iran General License DD, which provides a 15-day wind-down authorization for certain previously authorized activities through September 23, 2026. This move significantly impacts the Iranian aviation sector and related international operations.

articles.headline: OFSI Designates Al-Qard Al-Hasan for Supporting Hizballah

AQAH is deemed an involved person due to its association with Hizballah, an entity involved in terrorist activity.

OFSI's statement of reasons indicates that AQAH is involved in providing financial services and making funds available for the purposes of terrorism, specifically to Hizballah. This designation imposes an asset freeze and director disqualification sanction on AQAH.
This action prohibits making funds or economic resources available to AQAH and requires any person in possession or control of AQAH's funds or economic resources to freeze them and report to OFSI.

articles.headline: EU Strengthens Iran Sanctions Regime, Widening Scope Beyond Nuclear Proliferation
body: Brussels has reworked and strengthened its Iran sanctions regime, with changes largely passing unnoticed due to the EU's focus on Russia. The updated sanctions, effective after September 2025, have expanded beyond their previous focus on nuclear goods, missile-relevant equipment, drone production, and telecommunications.

The broadened scope now includes the maritime and shipping sectors, goods used in oil and gas production, and basic military and industrial items. This alignment with U.S. sanctions policy indicates a more comprehensive approach to restricting Iran's economic and military capabilities.

The EU had previously expanded its sanctions framework in May 2024 to ban the sale of missile components, in addition to the ban on unmanned aerial vehicle components adopted in July 2023, specifically targeting Iran's military support for Russia's war against Ukraine.

articles.headline: UK Expands Iran Sanctions to Tackle Nuclear Activity and Hostile Actions
body: The United Kingdom has laid legislation to expand its sanctions regime against Iran, aiming to tackle Iranian nuclear activity and other hostile actions. The new Iran (Sanctions) (Amendment) Regulations 2026 will amend existing regulations to introduce sectoral measures, broadly those lifted as part of the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action.

The legislation expands trade prohibitions against Iran to include additional goods, technology, and services crucial to industries contributing to Iranian nuclear escalation, such as energy, software, metals, gold, and related activities like shipping, insurance, and banking. It also prohibits the export of additional goods and technology key to Iran's conventional weapons and nuclear capabilities.

Furthermore, Iranian aircraft will be prohibited from landing in the UK, with certain exemptions, and the legislation strengthens powers to sanction ships enabling and facilitating Iran's nuclear program and destabilizing behavior.

articles.headline: OCC and FDIC Finalize Rule Redefining 'Unsafe or Unsound Practices' and MRA Standards
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) have finalized a joint rule that redefines 'unsafe or unsound practices' and establishes new standards for Matters Requiring Attention (MRAs). This rule, published in the Federal Register on September 1, 2026, aims to refocus supervision on material financial risks.

The new definition for an unsafe or unsound practice requires it to be contrary to generally accepted standards of prudent operation and likely to materially harm the institution's financial condition or present a material risk of loss to the Deposit Insurance Fund (DIF), or have already caused material harm.

The OCC has also revised its policies and procedures manuals regarding enforcement actions and MRAs, emphasizing material financial risks and highlighting principles of escalation, tailoring, and focusing corrective actions on essential deficiencies. The rule is effective November 2, 2026.

articles.headline: FinCEN Issues Alert to Counter Iranian Procurement Efforts for Commercial Aviation Industry

This alert aims to raise awareness about potential illicit financing activities related to Iran's attempts to acquire goods and services for its aviation sector, which may be subject to U.S. sanctions.

The alert provides guidance on red flags and indicators of suspicious activity that financial institutions should monitor to prevent their services from being exploited by Iranian entities seeking to circumvent sanctions. This is part of FinCEN's ongoing efforts to safeguard the financial system from illicit activity and counter the financing of terrorism.
This action complements broader U.S. sanctions against Iran, which target various sectors of its economy due to its support for terrorism, nuclear program, and human rights violations.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian Entities and Issues New General License
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on September 4, 2026. Concurrently, OFAC issued Iran General License CC, which authorizes the wind down of transactions involving certain persons blocked on this date.

Among the entities added to OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List is GOLDEN GLOBAL PORTFOY YONETIMI ANONIM SIRKETI, a financial and insurance activities company located in Istanbul, Turkey. This designation is linked to GOLDEN GLOBAL YATIRIM BANKASI ANONIM SIRKETI.

These actions are part of a broader campaign, dubbed "Operation Economic Outcast," which OFAC has characterized as an "economic D-Day" against Iran, aiming to close every financial resource supporting the Iranian regime.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Entities, Issues New General License
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and the issuance of Iran General License CC, 'Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving Certain Persons Blocked on September 4, 2026.' This action is part of a broader campaign against Iran, which OFAC has characterized as an 'economic D-Day' to close financial resources supporting the Iranian government.

The new designations target entities, individuals, and vessels across multiple jurisdictions that are deemed to enable the Iranian regime's activities, including illicit nuclear and missile technology procurement, cyber operations, and oil-revenue generation networks. OFAC also suspended several general licenses that previously authorized certain remittance payments to Iran and Iranian access to the U.S. cultural and academic system.

In conjunction with these measures, OFAC issued updated guidance on the sanctions risks associated with Iranian demands for 'toll' payments and other requirements imposed in connection with passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates New Iran-Related Entities and Issues General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) of the U.S. Department of the Treasury today announced new Iran-related designations.
These designations are accompanied by the issuance of a new Iran-related General License, which may provide certain authorizations related to the newly sanctioned entities or activities.
The action underscores the ongoing U.S. strategy to exert economic pressure on Iran through targeted sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements New Iran-Related Designations and General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and the issuance of a new Iran-related General License on September 4, 2026. This action continues the U.S. government's strategy of applying economic pressure on entities and individuals associated with the Iranian regime. The specifics of the designated entities and the scope of the new general license were detailed in the official announcement.

These measures are part of ongoing efforts to address activities deemed contrary to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. The issuance of a new general license often aims to mitigate unintended humanitarian impacts or facilitate certain authorized transactions while maintaining the broader sanctions framework.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Turkish Bank and Subsidiaries for Facilitating Iran's IRGC-Qods Force Transactions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has sanctioned Türkiye-based Golden Global Yatirim Bankasi Anonim Sirketi (Golden Global Investment Bank) and its subsidiaries, Golden Global Portfoy Yonetimi Anonim Sirketi and Golden Global Varlik Kiralama Anonim Sirketi. These entities are accused of facilitating tens of millions of dollars in transactions for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF) and providing the Iranian regime with access to international correspondent banking services.
This action, taken under Executive Order 13902 as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' targets a critical financial channel used by Iran to move funds through the international financial system.

In connection with these designations, OFAC issued Iran General License CC, authorizing the wind-down of transactions involving the newly blocked persons until September 19, 2026. OFAC also updated its Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Turkish Bank for Facilitating Iran's Access to International Banking
body: On September 4, 2026, OFAC designated Türkiye-based Golden Global Yatirim Bankasi Anonim Sirketi (Golden Global Bank) and two subsidiaries for facilitating tens of millions of dollars' worth of transactions for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF).
According to OFAC, Golden Global Bank was established to provide correspondent banking services to Iranian financial institutions to enable China's purchases of Iranian oil.
OFAC simultaneously issued General License CC, authorizing certain wind-down transactions involving Golden Global Bank and its subsidiaries until September 19, 2026.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Iran-Related Designations and Issuance of General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations, targeting individuals and entities involved in activities that support the Iranian regime. This action is part of the U.S. government's ongoing strategy to exert economic pressure on Iran.

Alongside these designations, OFAC also issued a new Iran-related General License. This license aims to authorize certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited, often to facilitate humanitarian aid or other specific activities deemed to be in the U.S. national interest.
These measures demonstrate OFAC's continued focus on disrupting illicit Iranian networks while also providing mechanisms for legitimate activities to proceed under strict conditions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Turkish Bank and Subsidiaries for Iran Sanctions Evasion
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated Türkiye-based Golden Global Yatirim Bankasi Anonim Sirketi (Golden Global Bank) and its two subsidiaries, Golden Global Varlik Kiralama Anonim Sirketi and Golden Global Portfoy Yonetimi Anonim Sirketi, for facilitating Iran's access to international banking channels.

Treasury stated that Golden Global Bank was established to enable Iran to transfer oil revenue from China to Türkiye for conversion to cash and gold, and knowingly offered correspondent banking services to Iranian financial institutions.
OFAC simultaneously issued Iran General License CC, authorizing certain wind-down transactions involving Golden Global Bank and its subsidiaries until September 19, 2026.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC issued a new Iran-related General License. This license likely provides specific authorizations for certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited, offering limited exceptions to the broader sanctions regime.

body: On September 4, 2026, the United Nations Security Council Committee pursuant to resolutions 1267 (1999), 1989 (2011), and 2253 (2015) concerning ISIL (Da'esh), Al-Qaida, and associated individuals, groups, undertakings, and entities, enacted amendments to its Sanctions List.

These amendments, specified with strikethrough and underline in the entries, affect individuals and entities subject to the assets freeze, travel ban, and arms embargo outlined in Security Council resolution 2734 (2024). articles.headline: OFAC Designates Turkish Financial Institutions for Iran Sanctions Evasion, Issues New GL
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has designated three Turkish financial institutions—GOLDEN GLOBAL PORTFOY YONETIMI ANONIM SIRKETI, GOLDEN GLOBAL YATIRIM BANKASI ANONIM SIRKETI, and GOLDEN GLOBAL VARLIK KIRALAMA ANONIM SIRKETI—for their role in facilitating Iran's access to the global financial system. These designations are part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' a campaign to sever Iran's financial lifelines.

These entities, all linked to Golden Global Yatirim Bankasi Anonim Sirketi, were added to OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List under Executive Order 13902, which targets sectors of the Iranian economy. The action underscores the U.S. commitment to preventing Iran from using foreign financial institutions to evade sanctions.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC has issued Iran General License CC, which authorizes the wind-down of transactions involving the newly blocked persons. This provides a limited period for non-U.S. persons to cease activities with the designated entities without facing sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iran-Related Entities and Issues New General License Under Operation Economic Outcast
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' a campaign characterized as an 'economic D-Day' against Iran. This action follows OFAC's earlier 'Economic Fury' campaign.

OFAC issued a determination pursuant to Executive Order 13902, targeting five additional sectors of the Iranian economy for secondary sanctions: aviation, digital asset, gold, shipping, and technology. These sectors now join the previously identified financial and petroleum and petrochemical sectors under EO 13902.

Alongside these designations, OFAC issued a new Iran-related General License. This general license aims to provide specific authorizations for certain transactions, though details of its scope were not immediately available.

articles.headline: OFAC Sanctions Turkish Golden Global Bank and Subsidiaries for Facilitating Iran's Access to International Banking
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated Türkiye-based Golden Global Yatirim Bankasi Anonim Sirketi (Golden Global Bank) and its two Türkiye-based subsidiaries, Golden Global Varlik Kiralama Anonim Sirketi and Golden Global Portfoy Yonetimi Anonim Sirketi. body: Some Chinese rare earth suppliers have reportedly ceased shipments to the United States since early August, fearing repercussions from Beijing amidst escalating geopolitical tensions. This move highlights ongoing U.S. concerns about access to these critical materials ahead of President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington on September 24.

The halt in shipments follows China's imposition of sanctions on the Responsible Business Alliance (RBA), a U.S. supply chain monitor. Chinese companies are wary of potential punishment from Beijing for complying with due diligence frameworks like the Responsible Minerals Initiative (RMI), which is connected to the RBA.

U.S. officials have repeatedly urged China to uphold commitments made in Busan and Beijing over the past year to ensure the smooth flow of rare earth export licenses. The persistence of this issue has placed it high on the U.S. agenda for the upcoming summit.

body: Chairmen and Ranking Members from the House Select Committee on China and the Congressional-Executive Commission on China have sent a letter to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin, requesting a briefing on the implementation of the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA).

The lawmakers emphasized that the UFLPA was enacted to prevent goods made with forced labor from entering U.S. commerce, thereby ensuring American consumers are not complicit in atrocities in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region (XUAR). They expressed concerns about recent enforcement trends, including reports of declining detention activity in high-risk sectors.

articles.headline: U.S. Plans Targeted Semiconductor Tariffs with Domestic Production Incentives
body: U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick announced the preparation of 'targeted semiconductor tariffs' that will impose different rates based on whether production occurs domestically. Companies building production facilities in the U.S. would receive tariff exemptions or reductions, while those producing overseas and selling to the U.S. market would face tariffs.

Lutnick stated that the basic policy is: 'If you produce in the U.S., you pay no tariffs. But if you don't produce here, be prepared to pay tariffs to enter the world's greatest market.' He confirmed that tariffs would be linked to domestic production investments.

The U.S. government is reportedly considering expanding tariff targets beyond semiconductors to include finished products containing them, such as laptops, game consoles, and data center servers. Specific tariff rates, implementation timelines, and exemption criteria are still being finalized.

articles.headline: Global Central Banks Grapple with Inflation Amidst Geopolitical Tensions
body: Central banks worldwide are facing renewed challenges in managing inflation, largely driven by escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and their impact on energy prices. The European Central Bank (ECB) is widely expected to raise its deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% on September 10, with ING characterizing it as an 'insurance-style' increase to reinforce credibility.

The Bank of Canada (BoC) has maintained its overnight rate at 2.25% but signaled potential future increases if inflation broadens beyond energy-driven pressures. Meanwhile, Federal Reserve officials, including Governor Christopher Waller, are closely watching August inflation data, with a rate hike at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting remaining a strong possibility if inflation remains elevated. The Bank of Japan (BoJ) is also leaning towards a quarter-point increase at its September 18 meeting, which would take its benchmark rate to 1.25%.

The current inflationary surge, particularly in the Eurozone, is primarily attributed to adverse energy supply shocks stemming from the Middle East conflict and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, contrasting with the more multifaceted causes of the 2021-22 inflation surge. This shift in inflation drivers is influencing central banks' monetary policy responses, with a more gradual approach being observed in the current episode compared to the forceful rate hikes of 2021-22.
articles.source: Reuters / European Central Bank / Anadolu Ajansı

articles.headline: Oil Prices Remain Elevated Amid Renewed U.S.-Iran Hostilities and Strait of Hormuz Disruptions
body: Global oil prices continue to trade at elevated levels, with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) near $90 and Brent crude closing above $95, driven by renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities and ongoing disruptions to shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. The heightened tensions in the Middle East are keeping supply risks in sharp focus for energy markets.

U.S. President Donald Trump has indicated that the renewed campaign against Iran would not be prolonged but warned of preparedness for further strikes. Concurrently, U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has extended troop deployment timelines across the Middle East, suggesting the conflict could extend into 2027.

The persistent high energy prices are a significant factor contributing to global inflation concerns, with central banks acknowledging their impact on headline inflation figures. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil transit, is a primary driver of these energy supply shocks.
articles.source: Reuters / The Guardian / European Central Bank

articles.headline: Congressional Committees Back DHS Enforcement of Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act
body: Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China (SCC) and Chairman Chris Smith of the Congressional Executive Commission on China (CECC) have sent a letter to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin, requesting a briefing on DHS's implementation of the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA).

The lawmakers emphasized that Congress enacted the UFLPA to ensure that goods made with forced labor, particularly those from the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region (XUAR), do not enter U.S. commerce. They stressed that strong enforcement protects human rights, supports American workers, and prevents U.S. businesses from being undercut by illegal trade practices.

This request follows the Trump administration's significant expansion of the UFLPA Entity List in July 2026, adding 43 Chinese companies. The letter requests a briefing within 30 days on DHS, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), and Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force enforcement priorities across high-risk sectors.

Under the agreement, Venezuela's interim authorities granted North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP), a privately held Venezuelan oil producer, 100-year concessions for 17 oil fields.

This deal, which represents approximately 20% of Venezuela's total proven reserves, follows OFAC's recent amendments to Venezuela-related general licenses, removing the U.S. governing-law condition from contracts with the Government of Venezuela.

articles.headline: Israeli Attacks Kill Three in Gaza as Far-Right Minister Proposes Palestinian Removal Plan
body: Israeli attacks have resulted in the deaths of at least three people and injuries to several others across the Gaza Strip. An Israeli drone strike in the Rimal neighborhood of western Gaza City killed one person, while two Palestinians, including a 13-year-old child, were killed in Beit Lahia when Israeli forces opened fire.

These incidents occur as Israel's National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir unveiled a controversial plan for the removal of approximately two million Palestinians from the Gaza Strip within seven years. The plan includes establishing a dedicated ministry and securing agreements with other countries to accept people from Gaza.

The initiative foresees the departure of 250,000 people in the first year, 1.1 million within three years, and around 1.9 million within seven years, according to the far-right minister's office. This proposal has drawn significant international concern and condemnation.

Analysts suggest that China aims for a stable and economically connected Iran, but not one whose confrontation with Washington forces Beijing to choose sides, indicating limits to its support.

articles.headline: FinCEN Identifies Nearly $13 Billion Linked to Digital Asset Scams Operated by Overseas Centers
body: The U.S. Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has identified approximately $12.7 billion in financial activity linked to suspected digital asset investment scams. These scams, largely perpetrated by transnational criminal organizations based in Southeast Asia, leverage vast networks of criminal actors to facilitate and profit from illicit activities.

FinCEN's analysis of 33,904 Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) reports filed between September 2023 and December 2025 revealed the scale of these operations. Criminals employ fake personas and social engineering tactics to manipulate victims, often leading to significant financial losses.

This alert from FinCEN underscores the growing threat of digital asset fraud and the importance of financial institutions implementing robust anti-money laundering (AML) programs to detect and report suspicious activities.

articles.headline: Citibank Fined £4.7 Million by OFSI for Russia Sanctions Breaches
body: The UK's Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) has imposed a monetary penalty of £4,732,830.58 on Citibank, N.A., London Branch (CBNA London) for breaches of Russian sanctions. The penalty was imposed on August 11, 2026, following an investigation into 970 transactions worth approximately £19.7 million processed between 2022 and 2025.

The majority of these breaches occurred between February and November 2022, shortly after Russia's invasion of Ukraine, and arose across various banking operations including payment processing, correspondent banking, and account restrictions. OFSI noted CBNA London's particularly high exposure to Russia sanctions risks due to its client base and correspondent banking relationships with Russian financial institutions.

While Citibank voluntarily disclosed most of the breaches and cooperated with the investigation, OFSI determined that a monetary penalty was warranted. The bank received a 20% voluntary disclosure and cooperation discount, along with a 20% settlement discount, leading to the final penalty amount.

articles.headline: OFAC Reminds U.S. Persons to File Annual Report of Blocked Property, Amends Venezuela GLs
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a reminder to all U.S. persons holding blocked property as of June 30, 2026, that they must submit an Annual Report of Blocked Property (ARBP) by September 30, 2026. Failure to file a complete report by the deadline may result in enforcement action.
Filers are required to use spreadsheet form TD-F 90-22.50 and submit the completed form through the OFAC Reporting System (ORS), which has been the primary reporting mechanism for two years.

In addition to the ARBP reminder, OFAC also issued amended Venezuela-related General Licenses (GLs) and a Frequently Asked Question (FAQ). These amendments likely provide updated guidance or authorizations for certain transactions involving Venezuela.

articles.headline: Citibank London Branch Fined £4.7 Million for Russia Sanctions Breaches
body: The UK's Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) has imposed a monetary penalty of £4,732,830.58 on Citibank, N.A., London Branch (CBNA London) for breaches of Russian financial sanctions. The penalty, agreed upon on August 11, 2026, stems from 970 transactions totaling approximately £19.7 million that were processed between 2022 and 2025.

OFSI stated that the majority of the breaches occurred between February and November 2022, following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, and arose across the bank's operations, including payment processing, correspondent banking, and account restrictions. Citibank London's high exposure to Russia sanctions risks due to its client base and correspondent banking operations with Russian financial institutions was a contributing factor.

CBNA London voluntarily disclosed most of the breaches and cooperated with OFSI's investigation, leading to a 20% voluntary disclosure and cooperation discount, and an additional 20% settlement discount.

body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued a reminder for the filing of the 2026 Annual Report of Blocked Property.

Additionally, OFAC announced the issuance of amended Venezuela-related General Licenses and an associated Frequently Asked Question. These amendments expand the scope of three Venezuelan General Licenses (GLs 51D, 54C, and 55A) to include authorizations for transactions related to Venezuelan-origin coal, including those involving the state-owned coal company Carbones del Zulia (Carbozulia).

The changes remove the requirement for parties using these licenses to include a U.S. choice of law provision in contracts with the Government of Venezuela, a move made in response to investment-related reforms by the Venezuelan government.

articles.headline: OFAC Reminds U.S. Persons to File 2026 Annual Report of Blocked Property and Amends Venezuela-Related General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued a reminder to all U.S. persons holding blocked property as of June 30, 2026, to file their Annual Report of Blocked Property (ARBP) no later than September 30, 2026. Failure to submit the required ARBP by the deadline may result in an enforcement referral.

In addition to the ARBP reminder, OFAC announced the issuance of amended Venezuela-related General Licenses (GLs) and an updated Frequently Asked Question (FAQ). These amendments include Venezuela-related General License 51D, authorizing certain activities involving Venezuelan-origin coal or minerals, including gold.

Further amendments include Venezuela-related General License 54C, authorizing the supply of certain items and services for coal or minerals operations in Venezuela, and General License 55A, authorizing negotiations of and entry into contingent contracts for certain investment in Venezuela's coal or minerals sectors. FAQ 1247 has also been amended to reflect these changes.

articles.headline: Brent Crude Hits $97 Amid Escalating US-Iran Hostilities in Strait of Hormuz
body: Brent crude oil prices surged to $97 per barrel on September 2, 2026, following renewed military exchanges between the U.S. and Iran near the Strait of Hormuz. Two oil supertankers were struck by projectiles on Monday while attempting to exit the strait, leading to increased concerns about shipping safety and global oil supply.

The U.S. reported targeting Iranian rocket launchers preparing to deploy mines, while Iran retaliated with attacks on the United Arab Emirates and Jordan. This escalation threatens the fragile recovery of oil shipments through Hormuz, which had reached approximately half of pre-war levels. The heightened geopolitical tensions and their impact on energy prices are contributing to global inflation worries and complicating central bank policies.

articles.headline: Bank of Canada Holds Rates Steady; ECB Hike Expected Next Week
body: The Bank of Canada (BoC) has maintained its overnight rate at 2.25%, citing subdued labor demand, excess supply, and uncertainty over the durability of the economic rebound. However, the BoC warned that upside risks to inflation have increased due to the ongoing Middle East conflict and new U.S. tariffs.

In the Euro area, a 25 basis point rate hike from the European Central Bank (ECB) next week is widely anticipated, which would bring the deposit rate to 2.50%. This move is seen as an insurance-style increase to reinforce credibility as energy prices keep headline inflation elevated.

While core inflation in the Euro area has been modest, the persistent high energy prices are a key factor influencing the ECB's decision. The BoC also noted that the key issue for policymakers is how long energy prices stay elevated and how far they rise.
articles.source: The Guardian / TMGM Daily Market Breakfast

articles.headline: Iran Attacks US Bases in Middle East Following Reported Deadly Strike on Wedding
body: Iran launched attacks on US bases across the Middle East on September 2, 2026, in retaliation for a reported US strike on a wedding in southern Sirik county, which Iranian state media claimed killed four Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) personnel and a four-year-old. Jordan reported dealing with 13 missiles, intercepting 10, while Kuwait experienced a drone strike at a residential complex.

These attacks follow a Monday incident where two oil supertankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz, with Saudi Arabia blaming Iran for the attack that killed two Filipino seafarers. The renewed hostilities have significantly escalated tensions in the region, with Iran offering conditional talks with the US amidst the conflict.

articles.headline: Germany Blames Russia for Leipzig Drone Attack; Ukraine Finalizing Drone Deal
body: Germany has officially blamed Russia for a drone attack in Leipzig, which NATO's Mark Rutte described as a new escalation on EU soil. European Union ministers are currently meeting to consider their response to the incident. Russian President Vladimir Putin has called Germany's accusation a 'grave mistake'.

Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that Ukraine is finalizing a drone deal with Germany following talks with Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Zelenskyy warned that the Leipzig attack represents 'yet another Russian escalation' and offered Ukraine's expertise and experience to Germany. This comes as Ukraine continues to intensify long-range drone attacks deeper inside Russia, with military sources aiming for 1,000 drones daily.

articles.headline: Federal Banking Agencies and FinCEN Clarify SAR Confidentiality for Customer Communications
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), alongside the Federal Reserve, FDIC, FinCEN, and NCUA, issued a joint statement clarifying the confidentiality requirements related to Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs). This clarification addresses how banks can communicate with customers about potentially fraudulent transactions or account closures without disclosing the existence of a SAR.

The statement reaffirms that the Bank Secrecy Act's (BSA) confidentiality requirements do not extend to the underlying facts, transactions, and documents upon which a SAR is based. This means banks can discuss the reasons for account restrictions or closures, even if a SAR has been filed, as long as they do not explicitly reveal the SAR itself.

This guidance aims to provide clarity to financial institutions, ensuring they can effectively manage customer relationships and address concerns related to suspicious activity while maintaining compliance with SAR confidentiality rules.
articles.source: OCC / FinCEN / Federal Reserve / FDIC / NCUA

articles.headline: FinCEN Reissues Order Requiring Transparency from MSBs Along Southwest Border
body: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) has reissued an order requiring certain money services businesses (MSBs) operating along the U.S. Southwest Border to report specific transaction information. This order aims to enhance transparency and combat illicit financial flows, including money laundering and terrorist financing, in a region identified as high-risk.

The reissued order underscores FinCEN's commitment to using its authorities to collect, analyze, and disseminate financial intelligence to safeguard the financial system. It requires MSBs to provide detailed information on transactions that meet certain criteria, helping law enforcement identify and disrupt criminal networks.

This measure is part of a broader strategy to strengthen anti-money laundering (AML) and countering the financing of terrorism (CFT) efforts, particularly in areas vulnerable to cross-border illicit activities.

articles.headline: Iran's Economy Grapples with Soaring Inflation and Currency Depreciation Amidst New U.S. Sanctions
body: Iran's economy is facing a severe crisis, marked by runaway food inflation and a continuous depreciation of its national currency, the rial. The grim economic situation is exacerbated by a lack of foreign exchange reserves and the impact of new U.S. sanctions.

In August, year-on-year inflation reached 84.4%, with the rolling annual average at approximately 65%. The price of vegetable oil surged by 383% compared to a year ago, eggs by 294%, chicken by 177%, and red meat by 148%.

The U.S. dollar reached a new record against the rial on Iran's open market in late August, trading at roughly 2 million rials. Despite these challenges, Iranian Central Bank Governor Abdolnaser Hemmati stated that Iran possesses sufficient foreign currency reserves and is prepared to inject up to $2 billion into the foreign exchange market to stabilize volatility.

Bond yields are rising, with the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield reaching its highest level since January 2025 at 4.79%, as investors pull back from risky assets and anticipate an October rate hike from the Fed.

articles.headline: Eurozone Inflation Accelerates to 3.3% in August, Driven by Energy Prices
body: Eurozone annual inflation accelerated to 3.3% in August 2026, up from 2.9% in July, aligning with market expectations. This marks the highest inflation rate since September 2023 and remains well above the European Central Bank's (ECB) 2% target.

The surge in inflation is largely attributed to a significant increase in energy prices, fueled by continued geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, particularly the ongoing war in Iran and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Energy inflation jumped to 14.3%, its highest since January 2023.

This data has strengthened expectations for an imminent ECB interest rate hike, with markets fully pricing in a 25-basis-point increase to 2.5% as early as this month. While core inflation, excluding energy and food, eased slightly, the overall inflationary pressures are expected to keep the ECB on a hawkish path.

articles.headline: ECB Study Highlights Energy Supply Shocks as Primary Driver of Eurozone Inflation
body: A study published by European Central Bank (ECB) researchers on Tuesday indicated that the sharp rise in Eurozone inflation since the outbreak of the war in Iran has been almost entirely driven by negative shocks in energy supplies.

The researchers, Kristina Barouskajte Grishkevich and Klaus Brand, clarified that their estimates show adverse energy supply factors accounted for approximately 90% of the increase in energy inflation between January and May 2026.
This contrasts with the 2021-2022 inflation wave, which was driven by a combination of supply and demand imbalances related to the COVID-19 pandemic and monetary and fiscal stimulus.

articles.headline: Global Markets Trade in Red as Fed Hike Expectations and Geopolitical Tensions Weigh
body: Global markets are experiencing a negative trend due to heightened expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike and escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Bond markets are under renewed selling pressure, and stock markets are falling.

Brent crude oil prices have surged back above the $90-a-barrel level amid growing supply concerns stemming from renewed U.S.-Iran military clashes. This rise in oil prices is stoking inflation worries and leading investors to pull back from risky assets.

The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield has reached its highest level since January 2025 at 4.79%, reflecting inflationary concerns and hawkish expectations from central banks. Major U.S. stock indexes, including the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100, saw significant declines.

articles.headline: Oil Prices Climb Amid Renewed US-Iran Clashes and Russian Export Ban Extension
body: Brent crude oil prices have been pushed above $90 a barrel due to growing supply concerns, primarily driven by renewed military clashes between the U.S. and Iran in the Persian Gulf. These conflicts have prolonged the suspension of energy exports from the region.

Further exacerbating supply concerns, Russia has decided to extend its diesel export ban through September 30. This move adds to worries about refined fuel supplies globally, contributing to upward pressure on energy prices.

The escalating geopolitical risks and rising oil prices are consolidating the likelihood that major central banks will restart their interest rate hiking cycles this year to combat persistent inflation.

articles.headline: Brent Crude Rises to $92.61 Amid U.S.-Iran Conflict, Strait of Hormuz Shutdown
body: The price of Brent crude, the international standard, rose 2.3% to $92.61, as energy costs remain high and volatile.

This surge is largely attributed to the ongoing U.S. conflict with Iran, which has effectively shut down the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint through which 20% of the world's oil is typically shipped.
Higher oil prices are pushing up costs across various sectors, from gasoline to shipped goods, further fueling inflation and squeezing households and businesses globally.

articles.headline: U.S. Imposes New Tariffs and Threatens Further Trade Action, Clouding Growth Prospects
body: The United States has introduced new tariffs and continues to threaten further trade actions, which are casting a shadow over global growth prospects. These measures are contributing to persistent inflation uncertainty and are being closely watched by central banks.

The Bank of Canada, for instance, cited new U.S. tariffs and the threat of further trade action as clouds over growth prospects in its recent monetary policy decision. This indicates that the trade policies are having a tangible impact on economic outlooks beyond U.S. borders.

The ongoing trade disputes, coupled with elevated energy prices, are creating a complex economic environment where policymakers are weighing the potential for increased inflationary pressures against the risks to economic growth.

articles.headline: OCC and FDIC Finalize Rules to Refocus Bank Supervision on Material Financial Risks
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) finalized a rule on August 27, 2026, establishing new standards for determining when a bank has engaged in an "unsafe or unsound practice" and for issuing Matters Requiring Attention (MRAs). The rule, published in the Federal Register on September 1, 2026, will become effective on November 2, 2026.

This rule aims to refocus supervision on material financial risks, moving away from less consequential concerns such as policies, procedures, documentation, and reputation risk. Under the new standard, an unsafe or unsound practice must be contrary to generally accepted standards of prudent operation and likely to materially harm the institution's financial condition or pose a material risk of loss to the Deposit Insurance Fund.

The final rule also establishes a lower threshold for MRAs, which can be issued when a practice is contrary to prudent standards. The OCC has also revised its Policies and Procedures Manuals to align with this new framework, emphasizing escalation, tailoring, and focus in enforcement actions.
articles.source: OCC / Federal Register / Crowell & Moring LLP

articles.headline: OCC and FDIC Finalize Rule Redefining 'Unsafe or Unsound Practice' and MRA Standards
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) jointly published a final rule in the Federal Register on September 1, 2026, which defines an 'unsafe or unsound practice' under Section 8 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act.

This rule also modifies the agencies' standards for issuing Matters Requiring Attention (MRAs), establishing a more stringent standard that prioritizes material financial risks over nonfinancial risks. The rule is expected to reduce the number of MRAs issued and those escalated to enforcement actions.

The new definition for 'unsafe or unsound practice' is a significant development, as the term has long been used by the agencies without a regulatory definition. The rule will become effective on November 2, 2026.
articles.source: Federal Register / Crowell & Moring LLP / FDIC

articles.headline: OCC and FDIC Finalize Rule Limiting 'Matters Requiring Attention' Issuance
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) have finalized a joint rule that limits when examiners may issue 'Matters Requiring Attention' (MRAs), effective November 2, 2026. Published in the Federal Register on September 1, 2026, the rule defines 'unsafe or unsound practice' and ties prudential criticism to material financial harm.

Under the new rule, both agencies will only cite substantive violations of law, meaning an isolated Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) slip may not draw a citation. However, anti-money laundering, counter-terrorist financing, and sanctions rules remain expressly banking-related, and systemic BSA program failings will continue to be considered substantive.
The OCC also revised its enforcement manual, PPM 5310-3, and publicly released its MRA manual, PPM 5400-11, for the first time on August 27, 2026, in conjunction with this final rule.

articles.headline: OCC and FDIC Propose Rule Defining 'Unsafe or Unsound Practice' and Limiting MRAs

articles.headline: Saudi Arabia Forms New Defensive Maritime Coalition Amid Houthi Blockade in Red Sea
body: Saudi Arabia has formed a new multinational defensive maritime coalition in response to a Houthi declaration of a maritime blockade against the Kingdom in July. This move reflects broader shifts in the geopolitical and security landscape of the Red Sea, where maritime trade and energy flows are increasingly intertwined with regional influence.

The Houthi blockade and subsequent attacks on tankers and energy infrastructure near Yanbu and Jizan occurred amidst a wider conflict involving the United States, Israel, and Iran, which had already disrupted the Strait of Hormuz. This disruption forced greater reliance on Red Sea export routes for Saudi oil, leading to a sharp decline in shipping traffic through Bab el Mandeb and increased insurance rates.

The formation of this 2026 coalition marks a departure from previous regional security frameworks, with Saudi strategy becoming more pragmatic and coalition-oriented in the face of acute maritime threats. Notably, Qatar, a former rival, appears among the supporting states, indicating a shift towards functional cooperation on this security issue.

articles.headline: OCC Revises Bank Enforcement and Supervision Policies, Emphasizing Material Financial Risks
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) has issued revised enforcement and supervision manuals and proposed changes to its violations framework, in connection with a joint rule with the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC). These changes, unveiled alongside a final rule on unsafe or unsound practices and Matters Requiring Attention (MRAs), aim to adjust regulatory burden and align supervisory activity with a risk-based approach.

The revised Policy and Procedures Manual (PPM) 5310-3, covering bank enforcement actions, now places greater emphasis on material financial risks. It sets out three guiding principles for enforcement decisions: escalation, tailoring, and limiting corrective actions to those necessary to address specific deficiencies.

The OCC will generally not take enforcement action under section 8 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act without first providing the bank an opportunity to remediate deficiencies through the supervisory process. Additionally, PPM 5400-11, covering MRAs, has been made publicly available for the first time to improve transparency, clarifying that MRAs will only be issued for practices, acts, or omissions that meet defined criteria and are tailored according to financial risk-related factors.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian Entities and Individuals in Latest Counter-Terrorism Action
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related and counter-terrorism designations on August 28, 2026. This action is part of a broader U.S. government campaign, 'Operation Economic Outcast,' aimed at severing financial lifelines to the Iranian regime and its proxies.

The designations target entities and individuals involved in illicit nuclear and missile technology procurement, cyber operations, and oil-revenue generation networks across multiple jurisdictions. The U.S. Treasury Department proposed revoking Banque Misr UAE's correspondent banking access to U.S. financial institutions, identifying it as a 'critical node' for Iranian access to U.S. dollars.

Additionally, Bank Melli was sanctioned for allegedly facilitating billions of dollars in transactions for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Qods Force (IRGC-QF) and its parent organization, the IRGC, and for funding Iranian-aligned proxies.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian National and Hong Kong Company in Latest Counter-Terrorism and Iran-Related Actions

These actions fall under both Iran-related and Counter Terrorism sanctions programs.

The newly designated entities, Reza Mohammad Taeedi (Iranian national) and Kameng Trading Limited (Hong Kong), have been added to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List). The Treasury Department stated that these additions aim to disrupt Iran's access to financial institutions that have facilitated the Iranian government's money laundering activities.

This move underscores the U.S. administration's continued commitment to imposing stringent economic consequences on any country or entity providing financial lifelines to Iran, as previously warned by President Donald Trump and reaffirmed by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
